root_idea.summary: A root oriented to loss and the yearning or anguish it produces, extending into grief, regret, and anger.
root_idea.development: The core notion of something being missed or lost develops into intense lamentation or regret. The same aroused emotion may appear as grief when directed upward and anger when directed toward an inferior; related extensions describe barren land and a person or animal that does not gain weight.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form.
Displayed as the noun أَسَفٌ, including its Quranic inflected occurrences.
Displayed as the adjective أَسِفٌ rather than as a generic noun.

senses.definition: To anger; to provoke to anger.
senses.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV; in the Quranic occurrence, the verb takes an object and denotes causing anger rather than experiencing grief oneself.

senses.definition: Grief, lamentation, or regret, especially intense sorrow over something lost or missed.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a noun of emotional distress; the Quranic occurrences include lament over a lost person and grief at people’s refusal to believe.
A Quran-attested interpretive value of أَسَفًا in one of its Quranic constructions; grief and anger are closely related but distinct realizations of the term.

senses.definition: Grieving, sorrowful, or lamenting; deeply affected by loss.
senses.usage_conditions: An adjective describing an intensely sorrowful emotional state; grief may coexist with anger in the broader emotional range of the root.
The adjective can express anger with or alongside grief, as in the Quranic description of Moses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To grieve, lament, or regret intensely, especially over something that has escaped or been lost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; commonly construed with عَلَى or عَلَيْهِ for the object or occasion of grief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be angry with someone or at something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; a distinct anger construction alongside the use meaning to grieve or regret.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to grieve, lament, or sorrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative use, distinct from the Quran-attested Form IV use meaning to anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiomatic expression of a hand, to become bruised, mangled, cracked, or chapped.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic, extended use associated specifically with the hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of an idol associated with Quraysh and the Kaabah sanctuary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name or cultic use, with variant accounts concerning the idol’s origin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deeply grieving, lamenting, or regretting over something lost; readily affected by grief and tender-hearted. It may also be angry while grieving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An emotional adjective distinct in form from أَسِفٌ; the emotional states may overlap.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slave, hired man, or socially insignificant person in a condition of subjection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transferred social-status use associated with abasement, service, or being scarcely accounted for.
A conventional status designation for one held in subjection.
An archaic personal-description use, also recorded in a traditional report.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who scarcely, or never, becomes fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use of the adjective without a restriction to a particular kind of person or animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land or a region: barren, thin-soiled, or scarcely producing vegetation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended or figurative application to unproductive land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Grief, lamentation, regret, or anger, especially in an excessive or intense degree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A deverbal noun from أَسِفَ, lexically distinct from the Quranic noun citation أَسَفٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state or condition of a slave or hired man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun naming the condition of abasement or subjection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The condition of land that scarcely, or never, produces vegetation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended or figurative noun use applied to unproductive land.

cautions: أَسَفٌ and أَسِفٌ cover an overlapping emotional range in which grief, lamentation, regret, and anger may be distinguished by context or interpretation; translations therefore vary.
The Quranic Form IV occurrence is specifically attested with the causative meaning “to anger,” while the related Form IV meaning “to cause grief” is broader Classical Arabic evidence.
